URL: https://ng.investing.com/news/commodities-news/gold-falls-below-4300-as-oil-fed-hike-bets-keep-pressure-on-bullion-2711087
Investing.com — published 28 September 2026, data timestamped 20:42 ET / 00:42 GMT inside the text. APPROVED FOR DATA ONLY per source rules; its interpretation is not used. Text via Exa search highlights.

Gold prices fell more than 1% on Monday, extending a weekly decline, as elevated oil prices and
stronger U.S. activity data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to keep interest
rates higher for longer.

At 20:42 ET (00:42 GMT), XAU/USD fell 1.1% to $4,236.33 an ounce, while Gold Futures dropped 1.2% to
$4,270.50. XAG/USD fell 1.7% to $63.24, while XPT/USD declined 1.3% to $1,758.04. The U.S. Dollar
Index was down 0.31% at 100.97.

The US-Iran conflict is now entering its eighth month, while Brent crude has risen about 70% this year.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said long term Treasury yields are being pushed higher by
stronger growth expectations, concerns over government debt and expectations for additional interest
rate increases.

Fed officials voted unanimously in mid September to raise the benchmark rate by 25 basis points, and
several policymakers have since indicated that further increases could be necessary. Markets were
pricing about a 65% probability of another rate hike in October.

The yield spread between 10 year and two year Treasuries narrowed to as little as 17 basis points last
week, the smallest gap since early 2025.

Gold has traded in a relatively narrow $4,230 to $4,510 range this month. Prices remain well below the
record high of almost $5,600 reached in January.

ANZ said the macro backdrop remains challenging for gold, with higher yields and a strong dollar
weighing on prices, though gold ETF holdings have risen by about 50 tonnes so far this month.

--- SECOND INVESTING.COM PIECE (oil), same date ---
URL: https://uk.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-prices-rise-as-iran-us-remain-at-odds-over-hormuz-reopening-4884580
Investing.com — 28 September 2026, data timestamped 21:09 ET / 01:09 GMT inside the text.

Oil prices rose more than 1% on Monday after Iran said it would not soften its conditions for
reopening the Strait of Hormuz, after US President Donald Trump rejected Tehran's proposal, raising
uncertainty over when traffic through the crucial oil shipping route will return to normal.

As of 21:09 ET (01:09 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in November rose 1.1% to $105.48 per barrel,
while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also gained 0.8% to $93.12 per barrel.

The Strait, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies moved before
the conflict began, has seen a sharp reduction in shipping activity.

NOTE: this piece also relays a Trump claim, sourced to Axios, that more than 20 million barrels
transited over the weekend. Axios is not an approved source and the claim is NOT used.
